draft.title: Landslides and avalanches
card: soil and rock sliding down a slope. Gravity pulls the material down once the slope can no longer hold it in place.
a mass of snow sliding down a mountain. It happens in snowy mountain areas.
Heavy rain can soak the ground, make it heavier and weaken it, so it may slide. Land clearing removes plant roots that help hold soil together, so it may also lead to a landslide.
Steep slopes make both hazards more likely. Both can bury roads, homes and people below.
draft.remember: Landslides move soil and rock, avalanches move snow, and both are pulled down steep slopes by gravity.

opts: A mass of snow slides down a mountain slope
A hillside of wet soil slides onto a road
A wall of seawater floods a coast after a quake
Hot ash and rock rush down a volcano's side
a.why: An avalanche is snow sliding down a mountain. The wet soil sliding onto a road is a landslide, because the material is soil and rock, not snow.
a.clue: Look at what is moving down the slope.

b.q: A farmer in the hills near Cairns clears all the trees from a steep slope. After days of heavy rain, the slope may slide. What is the best reason?
opts: Roots no longer help hold the wet soil together
Clearing trees makes the rain fall more heavily
Snow on the slope melts and starts an avalanche
Rain only causes landslides on flat ground
b.why: Plant roots help bind soil, and heavy rain soaks and weakens the ground. With the trees gone, the wet soil is more likely to slide. Clearing trees does not change how hard the rain falls, so that option confuses cause and effect.
b.clue: Think about what the roots were doing for the soil.

a.best: A mass of snow slides down a mountain slope

b.best: Roots no longer help hold the wet soil together

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about what the roots were doing for the soil' gives the answer away. The right option is the only one that mentions roots.

The remember line says both hazards 'are pulled down steep slopes by gravity'. The card only says steep slopes make both 'more likely', and it names gravity only for landslides. The remember line states this more firmly than the card does.

The option 'Rain only causes landslides on flat ground' uses 'only', while the card says rain 'can' cause a slide. It is a minor issue in a wrong option, but it makes that distractor easy to rule out.
